packs.title: Data freshness: options and recommendation (follows on from #12).
packs.note: Options for keeping the scheme data fresh, with a recommendation on each, and the decisions needed.

appendNote.text: 7 Oct 2026: options, a recommendation for each and the decisions needed are logged as separate 'Data freshness' entries. Recommended: build the weekly link and change watcher (A) and the AI-assisted comparison (B) first, then quarterly scheme confirmations (C). Nothing is applied automatically; a person approves every change.

items.title: Data freshness: agree the plan and build order (recommended: A and B first, then C)
items.details:
There are three jobs: (1) is the page still there, (2) does it still say what we say, (3) does the scheme confirm it is right. Automation can do 1 and 2. Only the scheme can do 3, because eligibility, capacity and referral changes are often never published.

Recommended build order:
- Phase 1: option A, the weekly link and change watcher (about half a day to a day).
- Phase 2: option B, AI-assisted comparison (1 to 2 days).
- Phase 3: option C, quarterly scheme confirmations (2 to 3 days plus decisions).
- Option D is optional.

Nothing is ever applied automatically. Findings become proposed changes that a person approves, which keeps the 'curated' promise.

Suggested cadence: link and change checks weekly; AI comparison on pages that changed, plus a full sweep monthly; scheme confirmations quarterly, matching the current review cycle.

items.title: Data freshness: should alerts to scheme contacts go out automatically, or as drafts Phil approves first?
items.details:
This is the decision that shapes the design.

Recommendation: start with drafts that the system prepares and Phil approves and sends. An automatic email to partners on behalf of an NHS-linked programme could land badly, and we don't yet know how partners will react. Once the process is trusted, automate the reminders, but not the first contact.

items.title: Data freshness, option A: weekly link and change watcher
items.details:
What: each week, fetch every scheme's web page and referral links, record whether each is fine, moved or dead, and take a fingerprint of the main text so changes can be flagged.
Catches: dead or moved pages, and changed wording.
Misses: anything not published online. It can be noisy (cookie banners, dates), so the text needs cleaning first.
Effort: small, about half a day to a day. Effectively free to run.

Recommendation: build this first. It also gives each scheme a 'last checked automatically' date.

items.title: Data freshness, option B: AI-assisted comparison of pages with our record
items.details:
What: Claude reads each scheme page and compares the phone, email, address, referral routes, eligibility and open or closed status with our record. It lists proposed changes with quotes as evidence. Never applied automatically: a person approves each change.
Catches: changes we would otherwise miss, with the evidence attached.
Misses: information that isn't on the page, and pages that need JavaScript (for example Eventbrite or forms).
Cost: a rough estimate of 15p to 35p per full run across all 17 schemes.
Effort: 1 to 2 days.

Recommendation: run it weekly on pages that changed, plus a full sweep monthly. That saves money and cuts noise.

items.title: Data freshness, option C: quarterly scheme confirmation
items.details:
What: each scheme contact gets a short summary of what we hold, with a simple 'all correct / needs changing' reply, plus reminders and escalation.
Catches: the authoritative answer, including things never published online.
Misses: nothing if they reply. The risk is people not replying.
Effort: 2 to 3 days, plus decisions on who sends it and from where.

Recommendation: do this after A and B, quarterly to match the current review cycle.

Suggested escalation ladder: change detected, then a digest to Phil, then Phil approves a drafted email to the contact, a reminder after 7 days, and after 14 days the card shows an 'unverified' warning (already built for old entries) and it is logged here.

items.title: Data freshness, option D: provider register checks (optional)
items.details:
What: check Charity Commission and Companies House records to spot a provider closing, merging or changing name.
Catches: the provider disappearing.
Misses: everything about the scheme itself.
Effort: small.

Recommendation: optional, and low value on its own. Consider it once A to C are working.

items.title: Data freshness: don't automate social media monitoring
items.details:
Scraping Facebook or Instagram breaks their terms and gets blocked, and the official APIs only cover pages you own.

Recommendation: leave social media out of the automation and ask scheme contacts to confirm changes instead (option C). If a scheme publishes news on its own website or an RSS feed, option A can watch that.

items.title: Data freshness: set up a private register of scheme contacts
items.details:
The repo is public, so the list of who to alert can't live there. It needs a private home, for example the team log's store or a SharePoint list.

Most schemes only have a generic mailbox in the data, and some have none (Employment Kirklees and REAL list only a phone number or web page). We need a named contact or mailbox for each scheme, and agreement from the scheme that we can use it.

items.title: Data freshness: decide how emails are sent
items.details:
Cloudflare's built-in email sending can only reach verified addresses and needs a domain we have onboarded, so it doesn't suit emailing partners.

Realistic choices: send from a programme mailbox (with drafts prepared by the system), or use a transactional email service (free tiers exist). Use a sender identity that isn't a personal address.

Recommendation: programme mailbox, with drafts first.

items.title: Data freshness: check the approach with the information governance lead
items.details: Emailing scheme contacts is operational contact with partner organisations, but run the approach past your IG lead, especially if named individuals' email addresses are involved. Also note that in option B, fetched web pages and our scheme records are sent to the AI service.

items.title: Data freshness: make the weekly schedule reliable
items.details:
GitHub's scheduled workflows can be delayed under heavy load, and they are switched off in repositories with no activity for 60 days.

Recommendation: add a heartbeat so we know each run happened, and optionally have a Cloudflare timer trigger the run. Keep a manual 'Run workflow' button as a backup.

items.title: Data freshness: show 'last checked automatically' separately from 'confirmed by the scheme'
items.details: Cards currently show one 'last checked' date, taken from the source document. Once automatic checks run, show two dates and be clear about which is which, so people aren't misled by an automatic check that couldn't see eligibility changes.

packs.title: Urgent support: contacts for each kind of urgent support.
packs.note: The finder now recognises medical, mental health crisis, domestic abuse, child safeguarding and adult safeguarding. Only the first two have specific contacts.

items.title: Add checked support contacts for domestic abuse, child safeguarding and adult safeguarding
items.details:
When the finder spots one of these, it shows 999 and NHS 111 only, because no specific helplines have been checked yet. They are not to be taken from a general web search.

Needed: for each of the three, the right Kirklees (or national) service, its phone number and opening hours, checked from an official source such as the council or the service itself, and agreed with whoever signs off safeguarding for the programme. Then add each one as a whole sentence to URGENT_CONTACTS in site/app.js. Until then the panel is safe but generic.

items.title: Urgent replies show no scheme cards: is that right for domestic abuse and safeguarding?
items.details: Decision so far: whenever the finder spots urgent support, it shows no scheme cards and asks no questions, whatever the kind. That is the cautious choice. A person facing domestic abuse who has also lost their job might still want to see employment support, so this could be loosened for some kinds later. Needs a view from whoever signs off safeguarding.

items.title: Import: test matching with all 168 schemes before the wider test
items.details:
The finder grew from 31 to 168 schemes on 15 Oct 2026. Picking the right 2 or 3 from 168 is harder than from 31.

Write a set of test scenarios with the expected answers (including the ones on the help page), run them, and check:
- HWL schemes still come first when the fit is similar
- national helplines don't crowd out local schemes
- money, debt and housing questions now get sensible matches
- condition-specific services only appear when mentioned.

items.title: The Suicide Bereavement Service never shows when someone writes 'suicide'
items.details:
Any message with the word 'suicide' shows the crisis panel and no cards, by design. So someone bereaved by suicide who uses the word won't see wy-suicide-bereavement in that conversation.

Options: accept this (the crisis response is the safer default), or have the crisis panel mention bereavement support when appropriate. Needs a decision with the safeguarding lead before changing anything.

items.details:

This stops broken scheme data, or unchecked edits by a future maintenance agent, going live.
